citation: Paller, V.G.V., Labatos, B.V. Jr., Lontoc, B.M., Matalog, O.E. and Ocampo, P.P. (2011). Freshwater Fish Fauna in Watersheds of Mt. Makiling Forest Reserve, Laguna, Philippines. Philippine Journal of Science 140(2):195-206.

primarySource.sourceLocator: PJS Vol. 140 No. 2 (December 2011), pp.195-206; study sites and sampling pp.196-197; Table 1 and results pp.198-199; water-quality and abundance tables pp.199-200.

access.reviewMethod: Read the full official publisher PDF through its web-text view on 2026-11-01.
access.priorDirectRequest: The earlier review recorded HTTP 403 for direct PDF/article requests; the official indexed web-text view is now readable.
access.screenshotAttempt: The official PDF screenshot endpoint returned a cache-miss error; tables were not visually inspected.

survey.reportedGeography: The article describes the three study sites as Laguna freshwater watersheds within the Mt. Makiling Forest Reserve; it says the reserve spans parts of Los Baños, Bay and Calamba in Laguna and Sto. Tomas in Batangas, and the three study watersheds drain to Laguna de Bay.
survey.dateLimit: The PDF gives a received date of 29 April 2010 but does not state the fish collection dates in the text reviewed; receipt/publication dates are not treated as field dates.
survey.methods: Randomized collection areas within each study site; seine nets, hand nets, fish traps, hook-and-line, and low-voltage backpack electrofishing. The paper says voucher specimens were obtained and deposited at the UPLB Limnological Research Station, but supplies no catalog/accession numbers.
survey.habitatAndWaterQuality: The paper reports measuring dissolved oxygen, pH, salinity and temperature. No salinity values or validated station-to-waterbody measurement crosswalk are transcribed here; no current water classification or safety claim follows.
survey.baitMethodLimit: The methods say earthworms were used as hook-and-line bait to catch rock gobies. This is a study method, not stomach-content evidence of natural diet and not generalized bait advice.

reportedResults.interpretation: Historical source-reported richness and abundance only. The article separately contains one genus-level Rhinogobius sp. label; source taxonomy and counts are not independently normalized.

qualityAndTaxonomyFlags: One results sentence says '4,920 species' where the conclusion and Table 4 describe 4,920 individuals; treat this as a source unit typo, not species richness.
The source's Table 1 contains a genus-level Rhinogobius sp. entry while the paper reports 16 species; keep the source total unresolved as a count of fully identified species.
Names and introduced/native/endemic categories follow FishBase 2010 and Catalogue of Fishes 2011 as cited by the paper; no present-day taxonomy or species-status crosswalk was completed.
Source spellings such as Poecilia latippina and Xiphophorus helleri require current taxonomic review and are not normalized here.
The PDF text extraction is not a visual validation of table cells or station-level presence marks.

reuse.policyFinding: The PJS Author's Guide says accepted authors sign a copyright-transfer form. The journal's open-access label describes access, but no item-level reuse license or permission for a structured public species dataset was verified.
reuse.disposition: Do not redistribute the species-by-site table or create public app rows from it without written permission and separate visual and taxonomic review.

scopeDecision.dampalitFallsScopeUnit: No separate Dampalit Falls unit is present in the current CALABARZON scope registry.
scopeDecision.reason: The source was already linked to Molawin Creek and Cambantoc River. Keep its field data held, and do not add a Dampalit Falls alias or separate waterbody without a feature crosswalk.

nextActions: Ask the authors or UPLB Limnological Research Station for voucher/accession details, field dates and site documentation.
Clarify whether Dampalit Falls refers to a separate waterbody unit or a falls/site on another named watercourse before expanding the denominator.
Request written permission if using the table; otherwise prioritize independently reusable species records and current taxonomy.
nonClaims: The 2011 survey does not establish present-day presence or abundance, a complete inventory for the reserve, or fish presence in Laguna de Bay.
A bait used by study researchers is not a natural-diet result or a Bangwit bait recommendation.
No water-quality safety, current salinity, channel geometry, fishing access or legal rule is established by this review.
